subject: spring-boot
summary: Explains the responsibilities of Controller, Service, and Repository layers in Spring Boot, how data flows through a REST request lifecycle, dependency direction rules, and DTO/Entity separation.
key_points: Controller handles HTTP request/response only; Service holds business logic; Repository manages data access.
Dependencies flow one way: Controller → Service → Repository — never in reverse.
DTOs and Entities should be separated to decouple API contracts from database schema.
misconceptions: It is acceptable to call Repository directly from Controller for simple queries.
Service layer should build ResponseEntity objects for the HTTP response.
Business validation logic belongs in the Repository layer close to the data.
check_questions: What is each layer's responsibility in the Controller-Service-Repository pattern?
Why should Controller not call Repository directly?
Which layer is responsible for transaction management and why?

fact_candidates: Each layer's responsibility: Controller (HTTP), Service (business logic), Repository (data access)
Dependency direction rule: upper layers depend on lower layers, not the reverse
practical_judgment_candidates: Deciding where to place stock-check logic (Service, not Repository or Controller)
Choosing whether to return Entity or DTO from a Service method
error_interpretation_candidates: Circular dependency error when two Services inject each other
NullPointerException from Controller returning null instead of proper error response
scenario_candidates: Reviewing code where Controller directly queries the database and identifying the violation
Tracing a POST request through all three layers to identify where validation occurs
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Believing skipping the Service layer is fine for read-only endpoints
Thinking ResponseEntity belongs in the Service layer
